data.narrative:
Dexterity is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon, Robert Sun, Kevin Chavez, Ben Varkey Benjamin, Talbot Morris-Downing, and Cuthbert Sun. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable across the robotics and manufacturing sector.

The stage-progression method was not applicable; the reported $1.65B post-money valuation appears inconsistent with the company's $104.9M total raised, implying a step-up multiple exceeding 20x that contradicts typical funding trajectory patterns. The peer-median approach, however, is applicable and anchors the analysis. Across five same-sector and same/adjacent-stage peers—including Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Humanoid ($1.4B Series A), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C)—the median valuation is $1.4B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

This peer-anchored analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B to $1.6B, centered at $1.4B. Key uncertainties include the reliability of comparable valuations in an illiquid, rapidly evolving sector; the maturity and commercialization progress of peer companies; and the sustainability of current private market multiples. The single public comparable (277810.KQ) was insufficient to establish a parallel public-market cross-check.
